units.title: SG-5.4.1 planPreload and resolveTextureKey engine functions
Act: Add planPreload to the engine
units.failure: Act agent reported ok:false: Created game/src/engine/planPreload.ts exactly as Step 1 specifies (PreloadPlan type, planPreload(scene, manifest) collecting object assets and dust effect assets, deduped via Set, split into load/unknown by manifest id). Typecheck of the new module is clean: no tsc error mentions planPreload.ts, and a throwaway import/call check (since removed) compiled. However, `npx tsc --noEmit` in game/ does NOT exit 0; it reports 69 errors that predate this unit and are outside its files: missing `node:fs`/`node:path`/`node:url`/`node:os` type declarations (tsconfig has `types: []`, no @types/node) in src/assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts, src/content/loader.ts and several tests/, plus pre-existing test-file type errors (e.g. tests/persistence.test.ts GameState mismatch). I did not change tsconfig or any test. Also, ran `npm ci` in game/ (node_modules is untracked and ignored). Note: planPreload.ts changed on disk during the session: someone added an exported `resolveTextureKey(id, manifest, fallbackId)` below my function. I left that untouched; it typechecks alongside planPreload. Fixtures: none planned or written for this unit.

tests.name: planPreload dedupes

tests.scenario: Given two objects both using asset 'A' in the manifest, When planning the preload, Then load is ['A'] and unknown is []

tests.name: planPreload reports unknown
tests.title: planPreload: assets missing from the manifest are reported, not loaded
tests.scenario: Given an object using 'Z' and a dust effect using 'Y', neither in the manifest, When planning the preload, Then unknown is ['Z','Y'] and load is []

tests.name: planPreload empty
tests.title: planPreload: a scene with no asset references yields an empty plan
tests.scenario: Given the validScene fixture with no asset references, When planning the preload, Then load and unknown are both []

tests.name: resolveTextureKey > known
tests.title: returns the asset id when the id exists in the manifest
tests.scenario: Given a manifest containing asset 'A', when resolving 'A' with fallback 'fallback:missing', then 'A' is returned
tests.command: cd game && npx vitest run tests/resolveTextureKey.test.ts --testTimeout=10000

tests.name: resolveTextureKey > unknown
tests.title: returns the fallback id when the id is not in the manifest
tests.scenario: Given a manifest without 'nope', when resolving 'nope' with fallback 'fallback:missing', then 'fallback:missing' is returned
tests.command: cd game && npx vitest run tests/resolveTextureKey.test.ts --testTimeout=10000

tests.name: resolveTextureKey > undefined
tests.title: returns the fallback id when no texture id is given
tests.scenario: Given no texture id, when resolving undefined with fallback 'fallback:missing', then 'fallback:missing' is returned
tests.command: cd game && npx vitest run tests/resolveTextureKey.test.ts --testTimeout=10000
